title: P33/P37: learned per-block ALiBi slopes (log-parametrized, init at the 1/4..1/256 table, NoPE heads fixed at 0) on the 115-fable hybrid-head Lean incumbent (4,800,024 params)
description: P33 (constrained learned relative-position bias) x P37 (different positional scales at different depths): the four ALiBi heads' slopes in each of the six blocks become 24 learned log-space parameters initialized at 115's fixed 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256, no weight decay, while the four NoPE heads stay position-free. 115 showed the slope table decides both the round-1 start (113's steep 1/2 head collapsed it) and the length frontier, so letting each depth pick its own locality in pretraining, and letting RL keep adjusting it on 7+ line proofs, should give expert iteration a better start and frontier than one hand-picked table.
hypothesis: The fixed table is a guess shared by all six blocks. With learned per-block slopes, lower blocks can sharpen toward local syntax (fewer malformed lines, i.e. fewer round-1 parse failures) and upper blocks can flatten toward content lookup (better citations at unseen lengths), and during RL the slopes keep adapting on 7+ line proofs, which a fixed table cannot. Risk: pretraining only sees cap-6 proofs, so learned slopes may fit short-range statistics (steepen) and hurt extrapolation the way 113's 1/2 head did; the logged final slopes will show which way they moved.
expected_delta: -40 to +35 dev solves at >=7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central 0); pretraining steps within -8%..+2% of 115's 4204/4218/4263 (six bias builds instead of one, grad through the SDPA float mask), val loss 0.077-0.085, round-1 targets solved 600-800

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid attention heads (4 ALiBi + 4 NoPE per block), CHANGED: the 4 ALiBi slopes are learned per block (P33/P37)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope, CHANGED from 115: additive per-head bias -slope_{l,h} * (query position - key position) via SDPA attn_mask, where for heads 1..4 slope_{l,h} = exp(log_slopes[l,h]), a learned (6,4) parameter initialized at log(1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256) in every block, so each block can make its ALiBi heads more or less local; heads 5..8 stay at slope 0 (NoPE, fixed, not learned). One bias per block per forward instead of one shared bias; -inf for masked/future keys as before
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: the fixed slopes buffer becomes model.log_slopes, nn.Parameter of shape (6, 4) (24 params), exp() then zero-padded to 8 heads, one bias per block. In pretraining it is in its own AdamW group at lr 1e-3 (same warmup/cosine) with weight_decay 0 (decay would pull log-slopes toward 0, i.e. every slope toward 1); in RL the frozen harness AdamW (lr 3e-4, wd 0.1) trains it with everything else. Final slopes are logged in stats['alibi_slopes']. Everything else byte-identical to 115
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state including log_slopes (6,4). The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged mechanism (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check with the pinned fork 51604b3 (vocab 100): 2-sequence prefill of 5 tokens plus 15 cached one-token steps vs the full forward, max abs logit diff 8.6e-7; backward gives nonzero grad on log_slopes

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm; CHANGED: plus log_slopes (6,4) in a second AdamW group with weight_decay 0, same lr/betas/schedule
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
